subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with an auth-profile credential, should the reusable-session auth epoch treat the auth profile as the canonical identity and ignore local credential storage presence, or should local file/keychain presence remain part of the epoch?
rationale: The narrow code fix is clear, but the choice changes the auth/session identity contract and must be owned by maintainers before automation writes it.

options.title: Profile identity owns epoch
options.body: Ignore the local Claude CLI fingerprint when an auth-profile credential is present, preserving sessions across file/keychain storage churn while still rotating on profile identity changes.

options.title: Keep combined storage epoch
options.body: Keep the current local-plus-profile epoch and accept that local storage presence changes intentionally reset live CLI sessions.

options.title: Backend-specific host policy
options.body: Adopt a backend policy that declares whether the host CLI credential or OpenClaw profile owns the epoch, then apply it to claude-cli with upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Profile identity owns epoch
recommendation.body: Ignore the local Claude CLI fingerprint when an auth-profile credential is present, preserving sessions across file/keychain storage churn while still rotating on profile identity changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history signal for CLI OAuth session continuity and session invalidation policy is Peter Steinberger's prior work on this exact surface.
